subject: Sandpit quality triage + next tests (AltScale comparative)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@altscale.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eval Team <eval@altscale.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jul 2028 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / follow-up - sandbox access + initial asks

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can prioritise the comparison work against our incumbent provider.

Summary of what we care about:
- Per-token latency p50/p95 for typical user prompts (short Q&A ~40 tokens; long context ~512 tokens)
- Hallucination rate measured against our 1200-case truth set (legal/regulatory domain)
- Cost per 1k tokens at production throughput (we're targetting 150 concurrent requests/minute)
- Degradation behavior under cold KV-cache / new session scenarios

Immediate asks from AltScale:
1) Sandbox creds + region with GPU nodes we can hit from our CI (prefer us-west).
2) Short set of reference eval prompts you ran (both generative and extractive).
3) A suggested minimal regression checklist we can run in the first 48 hours.

We can share our truth set (anonymised) after we get the sandbox details and an NDA addendum if needed.

-Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
Head of ML Ops, AltScale
liam.o@altscale.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@altscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jul 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / follow-up - sandbox access + initial asks

Thanks Liam — great outline and super helpful to see the evaluation priorities. Quick responses inline + action plan: 

1) Sandbox: attaching temporary creds (altscale-sandbox-creds.txt) and a small README with our endpoint URLs for us-west. We’ll spin up a dedicated sandpit cluster pinned to the same GPU class you flagged.

2) Reference eval prompts: attached is a compact CSV of the 30 prompts we use for initial quality comparison (mix of short Q&A, long-context summarization, extraction). I also pasted an excerpt below for visibility.

3) Minimal regression checklist (48h):
- Run the 30-prompt suite and capture p50/p95 latency, token counts, and full outputs.
- Run your 200-case truth subset (anonymised) and compute F1, exact match, and hallucination flags per our detection heuristics (we’ll share our script).
- Cold-start test: 100 sequential new-session requests and measure initial 50 tokens latency distribution.
- Throughput step test: ramp 10 -> 150 concurrent requests and note fallback/queue times.

I’m looping Marissa (inference QA) to coordinate the scripts and Neha (solutions engineer) to help validate the metrics. Proposed next steps:
- Monday: we hand off the auto-run scripts + evaluation harness (Drive link).
- Tue/Wed: AltScale runs the baseline vs incumbent and returns the CSVs.
- Thu: 30-min sync to review gaps, starter mitigation ideas (quantization, caching).

If that schedule works, we’ll also include a short cost-modeler sheet so you can compare per-request economics including cache hit rates.

Best,
Ben

--
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Intro / follow-up - sandbox access + initial asks

Adding the QA plan and a few clarifications for the eval team — tagging detailed items so we don't miss any edge cases: 

QA Plan (owner / artifact):
- Eval harness & runner script (owner: Marissa) -> runner: run_eval.sh (we'll provide Docker). Outputs: per-prompt JSON + metrics.csv.
- Hallucination detection heuristics (owner: Neha) -> heuristic script + thresholds (fuzzy match < 0.8 flagged).
- Latency runner with KV cache toggles (owner: Aditya) -> two modes: cold (KV disabled) / warm (KV preloaded).
- Throughput stress test (owner: Ben) -> k6 load profile attached.

Key tests to add vs AltScale incumbent (unique differentiators to capture):
- Prefix reuse / session stickiness: measure how effective Redwood's prefix caching reduces average tokens per request after session 5.
- Quantization quality delta at 4-bit: track token-level error rates vs FP16 baseline for legal extractive prompts.
- Automated fallback fidelity: when we fail to meet latency SLO, compare fallback model outputs' F1 on extraction tasks.

Data handling note: do not persist AltScale raw examples in public buckets. Use customer-provided anonymised files and our ephemeral storage.

Deliverables timeline:
- Today: Ben sends the creds and initial prompt set (done).
- Mon AM: I’ll upload runner Docker + scripts to the Drive link and a README for reproducibility.
- Tue: AltScale runs 30-prompt quickpass and 200-case truth subset, returns metrics.csv and outputs.zip.
- Wed-Thu: We prepare a short readout highlighting where Redwood is ahead/behind plus recommended mitigations (batching, quant profile) for the Thu sync.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Liam — thanks again. Quick note: creds attached in the first email (altscale-sandbox-creds.txt) and I've added the Drive link to the runner here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xEvalPlaybook/view. Marissa and Neha will be on standby to help with the runner if you hit environment issues.

Before you run: two small suggestions from our side to make the baseline comparable to production:
- Use the warm-KV scenario in one of the runs; many production setups will have session reuse and it significantly reduces cost/latency.
- Include the 4-bit quant profile run even if it's purely exploratory — it often shows cost tradeoffs relevant to your ops team.

If you can return the metrics.csv and outputs.zip by EOD Tue we’ll do an initial quick-pass readout Wed morning and keep Thu for a deeper discussion.

Looking forward to the results — let us know if you want a short demo of the fallback behavior and how we surface token-level cost.

Best,
Ben
